claims.statement: In subagent-driven-development a task may advance only after its Verify command passes and the single task reviewer returns both a passing spec verdict and an approved quality verdict.

SDD hands context between controller, implementer, and task reviewer only by file paths: a deterministic task brief generated by task_brief.py, the implementer report persisted by the controller to .harness-state/sdd/report-<task>.md, and a BASE..HEAD review package from review_package.py; history or report contents are never pasted into prompts.

task_brief.py extracts the plan's Global Constraints, the exact matching Task block (never a dotted-prefix sibling), only the Success Criteria rows named on the task's Criteria line, and the Interfaces line, and writes them to a path derived from a hash of plan path and task id.

The controller writes the implementer's inline report verbatim before task review, appends fix-dispatch reports under '## Fix round <n>', and on a BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT return writes nothing and removes any existing report so reviewers never see a stale report; an unrecognisable status is treated as NEEDS_CONTEXT.
For per-task review the package BASE is the commit before the task's first commit, never the branch base, and review_package.py refuses to run unless BASE is an ancestor of HEAD.

review_package.py adds STE lint BASE/HEAD hard counts (with synonym-rotation disabled) and scope-qualifier output for changed .md files under skills/, rules/, or agents/, and on tool failure or a 60-second timeout writes an 'unavailable' line while still exiting 0.

The task reviewer flags as an Important spec finding every changed implementation path not covered by the brief's Files list (ignoring specs/**, docs/**, and *.md) and every dropped condition, exception, hedge, or scope qualifier in changed skills/rules/agents prose.

The task reviewer's quality verdict enforces an STE ratchet: a changed prose file whose HEAD hard count exceeds its BASE count is an Important quality finding, and the quality verdict cannot be approved if a changed prose file lacks a lint line or lint is unavailable.

The task reviewer is a read-only agent that cannot write, edit, spawn agents, or run general Bash, treats cannot_verify as a non-pass, and returns spec_verdict, quality_verdict, a per-file meaning list, and findings labelled with checked_against.

The SDD controller gives cannot_verify one focused retry before escalating, sends all Critical/Important findings in one fix dispatch followed by re-review of both verdicts, and records Minor findings in SUMMARY and the ledger for roll-up to the final review chain.

On resume, SDD runs the source-tree runtime/resume_decision.py and uses the deployed .claude copy only when the source file is absent, treats any non-zero exit as stop, requires schema_version 1, and branches only on the structured action.

On an execute-plan resume, every cursor.checks_to_rerun Verify must re-run successfully before any pending task is dispatched, a failed re-run routes to repair, and required_transition is applied only after the session confirms its external condition.

The final review chain first runs diagnosing-bugs Phase 6 cleanup for a diagnosed bug fix, then runs context-propagation-audit only when the cumulative diff touches workflow-engine paths, then passes one shared branch BASE..HEAD review package to correctness-review and intent-review while keeping their oracle inputs and blindness rules distinct.

context-propagation-audit records a Source/Consumer/Context/Delivery/Proof matrix and fails when a load-bearing instruction's delivery is assumed or unconfirmed, child delivery is inferred from main-session behaviour, or an inline policy subset is unanchored; results go to SUMMARY under '### Context-Propagation Audit'.

Correctness review runs six isolated FIND angles from review-config.json, deduplicates candidates by (file, line), and scores each location in an independent scorer context that never receives the finder's reasoning or which angles agreed.

Correctness review findings must name a concrete trigger and wrong outcome; findings on lines the diff did not change are flagged unmodified-line and scored 0, which routes them to advisory rather than discarding them.

The correctness scorer uses only anchor scores 0/25/50/75/100, caps findings that rest on unreadable code at 50, and the threshold defaults to 75 with a floor of 60 so capped hypotheses can never enter the fix loop.

Correctness findings at or above threshold go to severity x Rule-class routing with at most three fix rounds per finding and immediate escalation when blocking findings do not decrease and the diff hash is unchanged; Rule 4 goes to ESCALATIONS.md and below-threshold findings are recorded as advisory in SUMMARY.

Intent review uses the verbatim SUMMARY '### Intent' block as its oracle, verifies any pinned intent.md with git diff --exit-code and stops on non-zero, and forbids the reviewer from reading PLAN.md or research-brief.md.

Intent review classifies findings as gap, drift, or excess, requires each to quote a verbatim intent sentence, reports SCs without a passing Verify Criterion row as gaps, and routes gaps and behaviour-changing drift to fixes or escalation, equivalent drift to advisory, and excess to report-only.

rules/review-policy.md maps each reviewer's severities onto a shared Important (blocks) / Nit (reported, never blocks) vocabulary and excludes generated files and wired-linter findings from all reviewers, and style/maintainability from correctness and intent review.

Before handoff SDD writes specs/<slug>/.review-receipt.json at the reviewed HEAD, and finishing-a-development-branch runs check_review_receipt.py with --require correctness,intent --require-audit-if <base>, stopping on any missing, stale, failing, or blocking receipt.

check_review_receipt.py rejects a reviewed_head_sha that is not a 40-hex commit SHA and treats the receipt as stale when HEAD has moved unless every file changed since the reviewed SHA is under specs/.
check_review_receipt.py fails if any recorded review has a result other than 'pass' or a non-zero (or non-integer) blocking_open, or if a required review type is not present with pass.

With --require-audit-if, check_review_receipt.py adds context-propagation-audit to the required types when base..HEAD touches a workflow-engine path and fails closed on an undiffable base; its regex is a copy of the commit-gate.sh workflow-engine signal kept byte-identical by a parity test.
check_review_receipt.py exits 0 when valid, 1 with a one-line reason on any failed check, and 2 on bad invocation.

Test seams reach the implementer and task reviewer only through the task brief: task_brief.py copies the plan's Global Constraints (holding the `- Plan-contract: 2` marker) and the whole task block (holding the `Seams:` line), and a test on the live gh-312 plan asserts both lines appear in the brief.

The implementer must write tests only at the task's declared Seams (skipped only when the brief lacks a Plan-contract: 2 line), write no new test when Seams is none, return NEEDS_CONTEXT before editing if a declared seam cannot observe the behavior, take expected values from a source independent of the code, and also test on real inputs of the seam's shape when they exist.

For bug-fix input, the implementer writes the red test at a declared seam targeting diagnosis.md's Confirmed hypothesis, commits it first, records red (exit 1-123 via run_at_commit.py) and green (exit 0) rows, and may write `Red test exempt` only when there is no testable surface or diagnosis.md and Seams both say none with the same reason.

The task reviewer's quality verdict flags as Important any new test not at a declared seam, with expected values copied from implementation output, using only synthetic fixtures when real seam-shaped inputs exist, or a task whose Seams is none (except a matching diagnosis.md `Seam: none` reason), and grants one extra focused read-only search per declared seam cited in search_surface.

check_task_review_contract.py pins exact phrases in task-reviewer-prompt.md (REQUIRED, including verdict vocabularies, checked_against, and seam checks) and implementer-prompt.md (IMPLEMENTER_REQUIRED seam rules), fails if SDD still references the retired dual spec/quality reviewer prompts, and exits 1 with one stderr line per problem or 0 with `task-review-contract: passed`.

test_check_task_review_contract.py verifies the checker passes on the live repo and returns 1 when checked_against, the implementer seam pin, or the reviewer seam pin is removed from a tmp_path copy; check_task_review_adoption.py aggregates the checker with task-review shell tests.

For a diagnosed bug fix, SDD names diagnosis.md in the fix task's Context, passes it to the task reviewer as DIAGNOSIS_PATH, and before dispatch requires the Plan-contract: 2 marker, a Seams line, and equal seam points between the first Seams entry and diagnosis.md's Seam value; on mismatch it does not dispatch, corrects Seams (normal lane) or returns to writing-plans (high-risk), and after a second mismatch writes a pending ESCALATIONS.md block and stops.
